subject: NovaRetail POC: econ and SLO approach for batching vs streaming
content:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novaretail.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: NovaRetail POC: econ and SLO approach for batching vs streaming

Laura — great to meet you and the NovaRetail team today. Quick recap from our call and two asks to get the POC scoped so we can lock a realistic cost target.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: product search and conversational assistant in store app (assistant used at checkout and by staff)
- Expected steady-state traffic (est): 30M tokens/day during peak season, average 8M tokens/day
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end under 300ms for checkout flows, 500ms acceptable for staff helper flows
- Security: VPC/private deployment likely for pilot, but open to hosted if we can meet SLOs

Two asks to confirm before we finalize the POC SOW:
1) Confirm budget range (rough band is fine) for pilot and next 6 months — specifically a target $/1M tokens you’d aim for.
2) Confirm how many concurrent low-latency requests you expect (approx RPS for checkout flow).

Initial pricing/ops options (high level):
- Option A (Low-latency, streaming-first): Hosted high-tier with streaming enabled. Pros: best p95, immediate low-latency experience. Cons: ~+20% unit cost vs batched throughput. Estimated unit cost: ~$22 / 1M tokens (streaming).
- Option B (Cost-optimized, batching + cache): Dedicated reserved capacity with aggressive batching and KV prefix cache. Pros: best $/1M at scale. Cons: higher cold-start and potentially higher p95 for tail. Estimated unit cost: ~$7–9 / 1M tokens (batched).
- Option C (Hybrid routing): Route checkout traffic to streaming-hosted or dedicated pinned low-latency pool, lower-priority flows to batch. Expected blended unit cost: ~$12–15 / 1M tokens.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm budget band and concurrent RPS for checkout-> I’ll run a short simulation to produce expected p95 at different batch window sizes and give concrete token/unit economics with our configs.
- We’ll attach a 2-week POC SOW with milestones (connectivity, baseline tests, latency profiling, price confirmation).

Attachments: draft POC proposal + latency-econ spreadsheet (attached).

Thanks — Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. A few data points from our side: 
- Pilot expectation: 2–4M tokens/day (we’ll ramp fast if checkout metrics improve)
- Peak season estimate (for later planning): ~35–40M tokens/day
- Budget band for pilot: $8k–$18k / month (we’re flexible depending on SLA)
- Target unit economics for evaluation: we’d like to see something <= $14 / 1M tokens in a pilot setting to make further commitment straightforward
- Concurrent requests (checkout flow): ~25–40 RPS during peak windows, median payload ~350 tokens per request

We prefer streaming for the checkout UX, but if you can show a hybrid that gives p95 < 300ms while staying near $12–14 / 1M tokens we’ll be very interested. Please include any requirements for VPC/private deployment.

Laura Chen
Head of Engineering, NovaRetail Inc.
laura.chen@novaretail.com | +1 347-555-0987


On Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:42:00 -0800, Vivek Kulkarni wrote:
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novaretail.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: NovaRetail POC: econ and SLO approach for batching vs streaming

Thanks Laura — that helps. Quick follow-up with concrete tradeoffs and a proposed instrumentation checklist so we can validate the numbers in the POC.

Concrete unit-econ scenarios (pooled examples for the pilot volume band 2–4M tokens/day):
- Hosted streaming (fast path):~ $20–24 / 1M tokens. Assumptions: streaming enabled, small per-request token sizes, no heavy batching. Expected p95: ~160–280ms (depends on model and region).
- Hosted batching (30–60ms micro-batch windows): ~ $11–14 / 1M tokens. Assumptions: continuous batching, prefix cache for repeated queries. Expected p95: ~300–420ms (tail worsens under burst).
- Dedicated reserved pool (4x GPUs pinned, KV caching): ~ $6–9 / 1M tokens at pilot volumes once reserved commit reached. Expected p95: ~200–350ms for tuned config; better tail if we pin resources.

Streaming vs batching: for the checkout flow (p95 < 300ms requirement) we recommend either:
1) Streaming-hosted for checkout traffic and batched for staff flows (hybrid). Blended cost target in pilot: ~$12–16 / 1M tokens.
2) Dedicated pool with small micro-batch windows (20–40ms) + warm KV cache. Upfront commit needed to reach $6–9 / 1M.

Instrumentation checklist for the POC (what we’ll need from NovaRetail):
- Representative request traces (sampled): payload size distribution, user think time
- Expected concurrency windows (we have RPS but want per-minute burst shapes)
- A test endpoint to validate network RTT inside VPC

If you confirm the $12–14 target for pilot and approve the instrumentation checklist, I’ll circulate a 2-week SOW and timeline. 

— Vivek

Looping in a couple of things we should include in the SOW:
- A KV-cache warmup run and validation step (to show cost delta with/without cache)
- A short canary that alternates routing for checkout 10% streaming / 90% batching to quantify UX delta
- Explicit test where we run the dedicated pool with 20ms micro-batching window to measure tail latency
- Line item for reserved capacity pricing and break-even calc for month-to-month vs committed

I’ll help draft the SOW language and the cost comparison table (I’ll populate with realistic kernel picks and expected throughput).
